text: Thunder star Jalen Williams rose up for a dunk, got bumped in the air, and came down on his left leg.
His foot landed flat, and then his whole body came crashing down on top of it.
Your lower leg has two bones. The big tibia carries your weight, and the thin fibula runs right beside it.
At the bottom, they wrap around a bone in your ankle like a clamp and hold it in place.
But when your foot gets stuck and your body keeps going, all that force twists into the ankle.
The thin fibula can't take it, and it snaps.
With one side of the clamp gone, the ankle bone pops right out of its joint.
That's a dislocation, and it's why his foot was bent out the wrong way.
The team said he broke his left fibula and dislocated his ankle.
Surgeons put the joint back in place and fixed the broken bone.
Now it needs months to heal, and the Thunder will check on him again before the season ends.
